# US Mint History

The United States Mint was created by the Coinage Act of April 2, 1792,
which also defined the dollar and established the decimal system of
American money. The first mint was established in Philadelphia in 1792,
making it the first federal building erected under the Constitution.

David Rittenhouse, the astronomer, served as the first Director of the
Mint. Early operations were slow: the first circulating silver dollars
did not appear until 1794, and gold coinage followed in 1795.

Branch mints followed in the 1830s at Charlotte, Dahlonega, and New
Orleans, driven by southern gold discoveries and the cost of shipping
bullion to Philadelphia.

See [[Philadelphia Mint]] for the original facility and
[[Mint Records]] for the surviving production ledgers.
